subject: Evergreen on‑prem support / retainer structure — pricing and credits
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel@hxmed.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@hxmed.com, techops@hxmed.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: On‑prem support approach and credit ask

Hi David —

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. We're very interested in Redwood for our on‑prem inference rollout (privacy requirements + co‑located GPUs). Procurement asked me to outline one open question before we draft an SOW: how do you treat the platform fee for on‑prem installs when a customer buys a multi‑year node commit? Specifically: can platform fees be amortized or converted to an implementation/ops retainer (we'd prefer capex treatment in our finance process) and what discounts apply to support tiers if we commit to 3 years?

Two constraints from our side:
- Finance wants predictability (prefer amortization or an explicit credit).
- Ops wants a clear support band (S1/S2/S3 coverage plus 24/7 oncall option) and SLA credits tied to response/restore times.

Can you share a recommended commercial layout (platform fee handling + support retainer vs per‑node support)? Ideally we'd get an updated proposal and any sample language for our procurement team.

Thanks —
Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Infrastructure, HxMed
[Attachment: HxMed_Rollout_Summary.pdf (8KB)]

From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Park <daniel@hxmed.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On‑prem support approach and credit ask

Daniel —

Appreciate the clear constraints. I looped in Naomi (pricing) and Marissa (customer success / SOW) so we can propose an option set that maps to your Finance and Ops asks. High level — two paths we typically offer for customers with node commits:

1) Amortized platform fee: we convert the platform fee into a one‑time charge that is amortized across the committed term and can be capitalized by finance. We then discount annual support by 15% on top of the committed node discount.

2) Ops retainer model: platform fee credited toward a yearly engineering retainer that covers runbook work, quarterly upgrades, and guaranteed incident wrap SLA; this is a service line item (opex) but keeps credits visible in the SOW. We typically price the retainer as 10–20% of the annual committed node cost depending on scope (oncall, runbooks, quarterly DR rehearsals).

I'll ask Naomi to draft a numeric example (3‑year commit) and Marissa to outline support bands and deliverables. Can you confirm expected node count (GPU nodes) and preferred SLOs for restore/response?

Best,
David
David Kim
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
[Attachment referenced: Redwood_OnPrem_Pricing_Proposal_v1.pdf (stub)]

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: david_kim@redwood.ai, Daniel Park <daniel@hxmed.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On‑prem support approach and credit ask

Daniel / team —

Attached is a worked example (see summary table on page 2). Key assumptions I used:
- 24 GPU nodes committed; list price per node = $X/year (linked in proposal)
- Platform fee list = $300k one‑time
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours, 24h SLA for response), Enhanced (24/7 monitoring, 8h restore SLA), Premium (dedicated SME, 2h restore SLA + monthly ops hours)

Two proposals:
A) Capitalization path (Finance friendly)
- Convert platform fee to a capitalizable invoice that is amortized 3 years = $100k/year equivalent.
- Support discount = 15% off list for Standard; Enhanced = 20% off; Premium = 25% off.
- No additional retainer required.

B) Retainer path (Ops preferred)
- Platform fee credited $200k to first year retainer, remaining $100k credited spread across years 2–3 as recurring credit.
- Annual retainer priced at $120k (covers 40 ops hours / month + quarterly DR). With credit, effective first‑year retainer = $ (see table).
- Premium tier includes guaranteed playbook updates and one on‑site DR per year.

I also included a suggested SLA credit schedule and a sample clause to allow Redwood to issue service credits vs refunds (helps with capex vs opex treatment).

Attaching: Redwood_OnPrem_Pricing_Proposal_v2.pdf; HxMed_MA_planning_sheet.xlsx

-Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Principal, Commercial Pricing — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_OnPrem_Pricing_Proposal_v2.pdf (22KB)]

From: Daniel Park <daniel@hxmed.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@hxmed.com, techops@hxmed.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On‑prem support approach and credit ask

Naomi — thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifications from Procurement and Ops after a quick review: 

1) Procurement: the capex route looks cleaner but they want the amortization schedule explicitly in the SOW and confirmation that credits equal a waiver of the platform fee (not a separate service charge). Also asking for a one‑time implementation credit if we go with the retainer path.

2) Ops: Premium tier sounds close to what we need, but can you confirm what "dedicated SME" means (hours guaranteed, escalation window)? Also we need a 2‑hour phone escalation path for P1 incidents during business hours, and 30‑minute response for P1 for Premium.

3) We'd like a sample DocuSign flow for a 3‑year PO + SOW bundle so procurement can map approvals.

If you can update the proposal with the explicit amortization language and a short SOW redline for both option A and B, we can push to procurement next week.

Thanks —
Daniel

Subject: Re: On‑prem support approach and credit ask

Daniel —

Thanks for the quick feedback. We've updated the proposal and included the SOW redlines for both paths (see attached). Quick answers inline below: 

• Amortization language: Section 2.3 now states "Customer and Redwood agree that the Platform Fee shall be invoiced as a single charge and Customer may capitalize and amortize that charge over the Term; Redwood will provide an invoice and amortization schedule for accounting purposes. Service credits applied under the Agreement shall be applied as offsets to future invoices and do not create separate recurring charges."

• Dedicated SME: Premium includes a named SME allocation of up to 40 hours/month with a guaranteed 30‑minute escalation acknowledgement for P1 and a 2‑hour on‑site or remote restore target. We specified SEP (scope escalation path) for work beyond 40 hours.

• DocuSign: we've prepared a bundling example that ties Purchase Order + SOW + Statement of Work exhibit A (SLA). DocuSign link included for the draft bundle.

Next steps I'd propose:
1) Choose path A or B by EOD Tuesday (23 Nov) so we can align SOW language with Procurement.
2) If you pick B (retainer), confirm whether the first‑year implementation credit should be applied as a one‑time invoice credit or as a deduction to the first retainer invoice.

I'll have Marissa follow up with implementation timelines if you confirm node counts. Happy to hop on a 30‑minute call with Procurement and Finance if that helps.

Best —
David
David Kim
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
